title: Medial and lateral orbitofrontal cortex in approach-avoidance decisions (Starkweather et al., 2026): SEEG high-frequency activity, 6 patients (derivative)
description: A BIDS-formatted derivative dataset of stereotactic EEG (SEEG) high-frequency activity (70-150 Hz) recorded from six patients performing an approach-avoidance decision-making task. It supports analysis of how medial and lateral orbitofrontal cortex contribute to approach-avoidance conflict decisions. The data are the authors' processed HFA epochs aligned to trial onset and button press, repackaged with behavioural variables, channel information, and trial-quality annotations.
methods_description: Patients with implanted depth electrodes (five at UCSF, one at WUSTL) performed an approach-avoidance task. Signals were bipolar re-referenced, band-pass filtered (0.5-200 Hz), notch filtered at 60 Hz and harmonics, and HFA (70-150 Hz) was computed as the mean of ten 10-Hz sub-band Hilbert envelopes normalised to a 10 s pre-task baseline. Trials were epoched at 1 kHz into 12000-sample segments aligned to trial onset or decision.
